session.question: In this fouling study, how did Actinobacteria relate ta the microbes on prepainted steel, and what other kinda microorganism was most dominant there?
session.answer: Actinobacteria were detected as part of the microbial community colonizing the prepainted steel surfaces, indicating that they contributed to the overall community composition on the material. However, the study also showed that the surface biofouling was not dominated by bacteria alone. Fluorescence in situ hybridization imaging indicated that fungi were the most dominant organisms present on the prepainted steel, exceeding the bacterial groups in abundance. (huynh2016investigationofthe chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-a8cf2960: The study found that the microbial communities colonizing prepainted steel were of low diversity and were dominated by several groups, including Bacillus spp., cyanobacteria, actinobacteria, Cladosporium sp., Epicoccum nigrum, and Teratosphaeriaceae sp. Actinobacteria were part of the community composition detected on the steel surfaces. Fluorescence in situ hybridization imaging further showed that fungi were the most dominant organisms present on the prepainted steel, indicating fungal dominance over the bacterial groups.
From Tran T. Huynh, Ili Jamil, Nicole A. Pianegonda, Stephen J. Blanksby, Philip J. Barker, Mike Manefield, and Scott A. Rice. Investigation of the microbial communities colonizing prepainted steel used for roofing and walling. MicrobiologyOpen, 2016. URL: https://doi.org/10.1002/mbo3.425, doi:10.1002/mbo3.425.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: In this fouling study, how did Actinobacteria relate ta the microbes on prepainted steel, and what other kinda microorganism was most dominant there?

Actinobacteria were detected as part of the microbial community colonizing the prepainted steel surfaces, indicating that they contributed to the overall community composition on the material. However, the study also showed that the surface biofouling was not dominated by bacteria alone. Fluorescence in situ hybridization imaging indicated that fungi were the most dominant organisms present on the prepainted steel, exceeding the bacterial groups in abundance. (huynh2016investigationofthe chunk 1)
